correctness.rationale: For q fixed, the fraction of matrices with a zero row or a proportional row pair is O_q(n^2 q^{-n}). On 2LI matrices, rank-one left multiplication by any natural-basis vector forces a singleton support relative to the original basis, hence every natural basis change is monomial. The group ((F_q^*)^n)⋊S_n has order (q-1)^n n!; summing nonidentity fixed-point fractions gives O_q(n^2(1-1/q)^n) from support-s permutation orbit and diagonal-scaling bounds. The sandwich between genuine algebra-isomorphism classes and monomial orbits on the full and 2LI subsets gives a uniform absolute error across coranks. Standard rank-k matrix count gives exact principal probability q^{-r^2}product_{j>r}(1-q^{-j})^2/P_{n-r}(q). Sum over all ranks needs the joint sandwich, not n times the individual bound. Fixed r yields q^{-r^2}P∞/P_r²; the perfect limiting fraction P∞. Independent finite-field F2 rank distributions for n=1..3 independently match principal exact matrix-count formula, NOT the unrestricted class-count asymptotics. The explicit proof, not small experiments, establishes the result.
residual_risks: The uniform error is absolute after normalization; no relative estimate for r growing with n.
The independent finite calculation checks matrix rank counts, not the large-n orbit squeeze.
